1.author: St. Gregory the Theologian
1.text: Gregory the Theologian's Oration on Pentecost is the principal patristic homily for the feast and is read in part at the Vigil in many Orthodox parishes. He calls the Holy Spirit's descent the completion of Christ's work, the moment when the disciples are made not merely witnesses but bearers of the divine life. The tongues of fire signify, Gregory says, that the Spirit comes both to enlighten and to consume, to give understanding and to burn away what is unworthy. Where Babel scattered humanity by confusion of tongues, Pentecost gathers all peoples into one Church by the single language of the Spirit.

42.author: St. John Chrysostom
42.work: Homilies on the Acts of the Apostles, Homily 7
42.text: Chrysostom takes the four marks of the apostolic community as the four pillars on which every later parish stands. The believers continued steadfastly, Luke says, in the apostles' doctrine, in fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in the prayers. Chrysostom presses each in turn. Doctrine is not optional for the laity; fellowship is more than friendliness; the breaking of bread is the Eucharist; the prayers are the appointed prayers of the Church. Where any one of these is dropped, the church that drops it falls.
